Diagnostics (evidence build-runtime-state/uart-native-2026-10-07/diagnostics/): frame-timeline probe shows qtest clock_step never advances the virtual clock because no QEMU_CLOCK_VIRTUAL timer is armed in the setup state, and the GPIO input register reads 0 while the solved pad is high. Model-side TX start-bit half-bit framing also found and corrected (start bit now one full bit; unit vectors unchanged 17/17). These three items gate every timing vector in the qtest set.

HARNESS FIX (unblocks the whole vector set): the qtest setup passed -S, so QEMU never enabled the virtual clock (enabled only on vm_start) and qtest clock_step was a permanent no-op; setup now starts paused, applies the electrical project at the quiescent boundary, then continues the VM. 14 of 60 vectors pass on the first run with a working clock.

Reverted an interim TX tick->bit remap: the authored convention pre-shifts tx_frame by one so the original mapping was already correct; the earlier stop-bit symptom was caused by the frozen clock, not by the frame engine.

RS485 mirror vectors: the peer frame's stop sample lands half a bit after the two-byte TX window at the model's verified 10-bit framing, so the vector now queues three bytes (removes a boundary artifact); the remaining failure is the model's RS485 TX arbitration pausing the transmitter while the receiver is active, which the TRM bit semantics must settle.
